title.narrative: Greater Port Vila Urban Resilience Project

description.narrative:
The project will improve urban resilience in Greater Port Vila (GPV) through capacity building, institutional strengthening, and the construction of two multipurpose emergency shelters. The project is guided by the Greater Port Vila Resilient Urban Development Strategy and Action Plan (GPV RUDSAP) which envisions, that by 2030, Greater Port Vila is safe, inclusive, resilient, and a vibrant economic hub based on sustainable development. About 53% of the total project financing is from disaster risk reduction sources. About 15,500 people in the municipality of Port Vila will benefit from the project, of which about half are women.
The project also supports efforts to recover from the impacts of the coronavirus disease (COVID-19) pandemic and Tropical Cyclone Harold through (i) preventive measures for health and social safety nets; (ii) a focus on the vulnerable, women and the "new poor"; and (iii) partnerships and investments that generate jobs and stimulate the local economy.

Output: Resilience in urban planning and management is strengthened Indicator: At least 95 government officials, of whom at least 40% are women, trained in urban planning, development, climate and disaster resilience, and municipal finance concepts (2020 baseline: 0) (OP 6.1.1) Progress/Status: A total of 98 persons of whom 33 were women (34%) have been trained in urban planning, development, climate and disaster resilience, and municipal finance concepts in four separate formal sessions from November 2022 to February 2024. Output: Resilience in urban planning and management is strengthened Indicator: Leadership and decision-making training provided to at least 20 staff in the MOIA and PVMC, of whom at least 30% are women (2020 baseline: 0) (OP 2.3.1, 6.1.1) Progress/Status: Leadership and decision-making training were given to a total of 23 permanent position staff from DUAP/MOIA (11 or 48% are women). All DUAP staff participated in various training courses conducted to support the strengthening of the agency. These capacity building activities include leadership training, urban planning, disaster risk reduction management, climate change adaptation, and gender-based violence (GBV) prevention training Data Source: Project performance reports, PVMC business plans, regulations, and participation records Actual value:

Output: Resilient urban infrastructure constructed in Greater Port Vila Indicator: At least three multipurpose emergency shelters include gender-inclusive design elements and features and offer information, training, and potential to be first point of contact in a GBV referral system and in triage for health emergency response (2020 baseline: 0) (OP 1.1.2, 1.2, 2.2.3, 2.5.2, 3.2, 3.2.5, 4.1.2) Progress/Status: The three shelters are still under construction. The shelters include gender-inclusive design elements and features that align with needs by women, men, people with disabilities during the community consultations. These include gender-separated toilets, menstruation bins provided, a laundry area for women's needs, two kitchens, a large sleeping space area, a standby generator in case of power outage and triage in the emergency shelters. The triage area will be used for counseling of GBV victim survivors and for women in emergency e.g. pregnant women.
Relevant groups were consulted, including the Department of Women's Affair and Vanuatu Women's Shelter to ensure women's views, concerns, and proposals are incorporated in the design and future use of the shelters, including the aim to make it as a first point of GPV referral system. Data Source: GPV RUDSAP, feasibility studies, appraisal reports, detailed designs, and project performance reports Actual value:

Output: Resilient urban infrastructure constructed in Greater Port Vila Indicator: By 2027:

Construction commenced in Q4 2024 and is expected to be completed in Q1 2026. Output: Asset management and institutional capacity strengthened Indicator: A dedicated major maintenance reserve account established by PVMC (2020 baseline: Not applicable) Achievement: Y Progress/Status: PVCC established the account, however, there needs to be a commitment that funds will be available for the O&M per the approved plan. The Mission discussed this with PVCC during the midterm review mission, and they agreed that additional resources and funding will need to be mobilized to cover O&M costs.
The Mission also requested DUAP and PIAC to discuss the O&M and asset strategy management plan with PVCC and develop an action plan to ensure that resources for shelter O&M would be available by Q1 2026. The action plan should include ensuring that the shelters will generate revenue once they are commissioned as stipulated in the project-financed O&M plan. The Mission highlighted that sustainability of project assets is a critical aspect that ADB that ADB will review when considering the proposed second additional financing proposal. Data Source: PVMC business plan, project performance reports, training records, feasibility studies, appraisal reports, and detailed designs Baseline year: 2020 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2020 Baseline value: N Target year: 2027 Target value: Y Actual value: Y

The CPS will also support DUAP in the procurement/selection of a local non-government organization (NGO) who will undertake the scope of works. The procurement for this work is planned for Q4 2025.
